input.sha256_scope: No image input beyond a zero-filled shape. Every case is synthetic layout, region, and span specs written out in the capture tool; the expected file is both the input record and the expected record.

upstream.capture_method: The pinned standardized_data was executed unbound over six synthetic scenarios with an explicit score threshold (so self is never touched) and a deterministic recognizer stub whose text and score depend only on the crop shape; its call log is recorded to pin the model-call order. Scenarios cover the footnote and lone-title relabels, hurdle replace/append/below-threshold, no-text and vision-skip re-recognition, the OCR fallback, region growth to a two-round fixpoint, supplement shrinking against a grown region, and per-mask-label supplementary regions.

limitations: The recognizer is a shape-keyed stub, not a model; the real recognizer joins in the end-to-end slice. The stub is mirrored bit-for-bit in the Rust test.
convert_formula_res_to_ocr_format is not exercised: this port runs with formula recognition off, so the formula list is always empty and the call is a no-op.

Python set iteration over block indices is mirrored as ascending order, which holds for the contiguous 0-based index sets this function builds; the hurdle dict keeps literal insertion order in both implementations.
Crops are kept inside the image, so numpy's clamping and negative-index wrapping are never reached.
